open_points.subject: runtime settings table
open_points.text:
each item with its type,
whether it is its normalization; every item optional at this level and absent when
unset
open_points.question: What metadata does the closed environment table hold for each item: type and normalization, type and requiredness and normalization, or only type and field mapping?
options: Each entry holds its type and an identity normalization, with requiredness always false at this layer.
Each entry holds type, requiredness and normalization, with every requiredness value false at this layer.
Each entry holds only its environment name, destination field and type because values are returned unchanged.
open_points.default_guess: Treat the malformed words as “each item with its type and its normalization,” make normalization the identity operation, and record no requiredness beyond optionality.

open_points.subject: runtime setting normalization
open_points.text:
Every item is text taken as it is set: no
trimming, no case or Unicode normalization;

### Hides

Environment reading and the per-item normalization.
open_points.question: Does runtime_settings preserve every environment value byte-for-byte as text, or does it perform a hidden per-item normalization?
options: Preserve every value exactly; “per-item normalization” means an explicit identity operation.
Apply normalization selected by the table despite the statement that no normalization occurs.
Remove normalization from runtime_settings and leave all form interpretation to configuration.
open_points.default_guess: Preserve values exactly and change the hidden mechanism to environment reading and field mapping.

witness.initial: REGISTRY_STORE_LOCATION is set to text with leading and trailing spaces.
events: configuration checks the resulting store location.
outcomes: runtime_settings returns the spaces unchanged, so configuration checks a path whose name contains those spaces.
runtime_settings applies its hidden per-item normalization and removes the spaces, so configuration checks the trimmed path.
witness.observer: The owner sees Registry open a different path or produce a different start diagnostic.

open_points.subject: no-default policy
open_points.text:
no default for any item (A17 rule 5);

A17: every start check of rule 2, in its one order, over the settings
`runtime_settings` loads as set — the service tokens of the services
`data_provider`'s rights table lists, all or none, the other items present,
each well formed, each secret at least the 32 bytes `data_provider` holds, no
two secrets equal — with the diagnostic naming the failed item and never its
value; that no default is applied (rule 5);
open_points.question: Which module owns the decision that no configuration item receives a default, and what distinct responsibility, if any, does the other module have?
options: runtime_settings owns preserving absence without substitution; configuration only refuses required absences.
configuration owns the no-default policy; runtime_settings merely reports set or absent values.
Both modules independently enforce the policy.
open_points.default_guess: runtime_settings preserves absence, while configuration owns the policy consequence that required absence fails; state those as separate responsibilities.

open_points.subject: configuration start-check boundary
open_points.text:
A17: every start check of rule 2, in its one order, over the settings
`runtime_settings` loads as set

### Must not own

Reading the environment (`runtime_settings`), opening or making the store
(`store`), probing the backup location (`backups`), what a token may do
(`service_access`), the credential check of a sign-in (`owner_sessions`).
open_points.question: Does configuration own and orchestrate every A17 rule 2 start check, including the backup probe and store opening, or only the pure checks that precede those delegated checks?
options: configuration owns the complete ordered startup workflow and calls backups, store and listener owners for their checks.
configuration owns only presence, form, secret and path-relation checks; another startup module owns the full order and invokes backups and store.
configuration owns the order but not the checks, receiving their results from the owning modules.
open_points.default_guess: Let a startup lifecycle module own the complete A17 order; configuration performs only pure configuration checks, while backups and store perform their side-effecting checks.

witness.initial: All textual configuration checks pass, but the backup location is not writable.
events: The ordered A17 checks reach the backup-location probe.
outcomes: configuration invokes or performs the probe as part of the start workflow it owns and reports the failed start.
configuration finishes successfully because probing is forbidden to it; backups performs the probe under a separately owned startup workflow and reports the failed start.
witness.observer: Module tests and the generated dependency graph see different owners and call directions, even though the owner ultimately sees a failed start.

open_points.subject: import transaction and confirmation id
open_points.text:
checking again at confirmation and, in the one transaction `operations`
opens, which appends the import's audit entry, having each record written by
its own module with its source identities and instants — `projects`
the picked projects with their objects and rooms, `customers` the Customers
it makes, `artifact_pointers` the pointers, the import as their publisher
(M05) — and, once they are written, the closure (M10) with the confirmation
id `operations` minted then, or nothing (rules 6, 7);
open_points.question: How can migration_import use the transaction and confirmation id owned by operations when operations is absent from its Knows list: does operations call migration_import and pass them in, or may migration_import depend on operations and request them?
options: operations opens the transaction, mints the confirmation id and calls migration_import with both.
migration_import imports operations and asks it to open the transaction and mint the id.
A separate transaction interface owns these facilities and is known by both modules.
open_points.default_guess: Make operations the caller and pass an already-open transaction and the minted confirmation id into migration_import.

open_points.subject: upload stream handoff
open_points.text:
An upload's bytes are handed on as the request's
declared length and its unread stream, never read or buffered here, so
that `migration_import` alone applies A19 rule 4 to them.
open_points.question: Through which declared dependency does owner_interface hand the declared length and unread stream to migration_import, since owner_interface knows operations but not migration_import?
options: owner_interface passes them to operations, which calls migration_import.
owner_interface calls migration_import directly and must add it to Knows.
owner_interface passes them to owner_sessions, which later supplies them to migration_import.
open_points.default_guess: Pass the declared length and unread stream through operations, which acquires the A16 locks and invokes migration_import.
